kicker: Power · EBITDA margin change in a high-demand quarter, Q2 FY27
title: Power demand jumped; margins fell at 7 of 10
dek: A monsoon 13% short of normal lifted Q2 power demand 11.5% and exchange prices 46%, yet EBITDA margins slipped at seven of ten listed power companies. October consumption then jumped 21.9% on a rain-hit base (Construction World, Nov 2026).

read: Volume was not the problem, as EBITDA still grew at 7 of 10; costlier coal and gas, largely passed through tariffs, swelled sales faster than profit, so a record-demand quarter showed up as thinner, not fatter, margins.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; October consumption: Construction World, Nov 2026

companies.name: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

notes: Margins are operating EBITDA over revenue from operations in the filed Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 consolidated results, as computed by Vantage; the ten are the large listed generators, transmission and distribution utilities and power-market companies, and EBITDA grew in absolute terms at 7 of them. Demand (+11.5% to 502 bn units) and exchange prices (day-ahead ₹5.72/unit, +46%; real-time ₹5.24, +49%) are as stated on IEX's Q2 call; JSW Energy cited a monsoon about 13% below normal and imported (API4) coal up about 28% YoY, and sold merchant power at about ₹6.9/unit. Reasons differ: tariff pass-through of fuel cost dilutes margins at regulated and fuel-indexed generators, NHPC's margin rose on 17% more hydro generation, while PTC (trading) lost surcharge income and Tata Power cited curtailment rising to about 11% of renewable output. Adani Power had no Q2 FY27 filing on the desk; SJVN is left out because its revenue more than doubled (base not comparable), and pure renewable generators (ACME Solar, NTPC Green) are not included; Torrent Power, CESC and Power Grid have filed results but no Q2 call summary. News hook: India's power consumption rose 21.88% to 159.76 bn units in October 2026 (Construction World, Nov 2026), partly because rains cut October 2025 demand; IEX said prices had corrected to about ₹4/unit by end-October.
